line 1470 | medium | hStdInput set to None; comment says it's deliberately NULL; but None might be interpreted as 0 (INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)? In C, NULL handle for stdin is valid; Windows CreateProcess expects NULL for no handle; acceptable.

line 1487 | high | On failure after job creation but before assignment, job handle is closed in except block; but if CreateProcessAsUserW fails, job is closed in except; if assignment fails, job is closed in inner except; potential double close? job handle is closed in both outer except and inner except if assignment fails? Actually, outer except (line 1487) closes job only if CreateProcessAsUserW fails; if assignment fails, inner except (line 1492) closes job; no double close.
line 1498 | medium | TerminateProcess called with exit code 1; if it fails, exception is caught and ignored; process might survive; but then handles are closed; process leak possible.

line 1512 | medium | log.integrity_label and log.granted_access accessed only if log is not None; correct.

handoff.purpose: Define _spawn_low_integrity_process function, the core of process creation with containment.

symbols.name: _spawn_low_integrity_process
symbols.note: Implements the full sequence: token creation, command line, startup info, job creation, process creation, job assignment, thread resume, attestation.

claims.text: a raw handle cannot be verified and so cannot cross the boundary
claims.why: The code checks `if log is not None: log.verify()` on line 1448, ensuring only verified handles pass.

claims.text: RE-VERIFIED HERE, not merely at construction: target and rights are checked on the handle at the moment of use.
claims.why: The call `log.verify()` on line 1448 performs the verification at this point.

claims.text: CreateProcessAsUserW takes ONE command line, not an argv vector, and the callee re-parses it -- so every element is quoted rather than joined.
claims.why: The code uses `subprocess.list2cmdline([str(a) for a in argv])` to produce a single command line string, as stated.

claims.text: CREATE_SUSPENDED so the child cannot spawn a grandchild before it is inside the job; resumed below, only once assignment succeeded.
claims.why: The flags include `_CREATE_SUSPENDED` (line 1459) and `ResumeThread` is called only after `AssignProcessToJobObject` succeeds (line 1489).

claims.text: A Low child cannot write %TEMP% (Medium), so a caller that wants a usable child gives it a TEMP inside a Low-labelled directory.
claims.why: The code creates an environment block from `env` dict with null separators (line 1463-1464) and sets `_CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT` flag.

claims.text: stdin is NULL, deliberately: a handle on the null device would be a SECOND inherited handle for no security benefit.
TIGHTENING ONLY. min() with the module ceiling is the whole mechanism: there is no argument that makes the blast radius larger than the constant at the top of this file.
claims.why: Both `processes` and `job_memory` are computed as `min(int(max_*), JOB_*_LIMIT)` (lines 1477-1480), ensuring caps never exceed the module constants.

claims.text: THE ONE PLACE INHERITANCE IS DECIDED. `inherit` is literally "is there an allowlist?", so there is no reachable state in which handles are inheritable and the allowlist is absent.
claims.why: `inherit = allowlist is not None` (line 1483) is the only assignment to `inherit` and is used in `CreateProcessAsUserW` (line 1484).

claims.text: THE LABEL IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED by the arrival of the caps. It is a coarse name, and the caps are not a coarse fact: `job_limits` below carries the LimitFlags the kernel handed back, which is what a reader comparing two ledger entries actually needs.
claims.why: The `mechanism` string is built from fixed strings and conditionally `+bounded-inherit` based on `log`; it does not include the actual limits. `job_limits` is included separately in the attestation.

claims.text: An old record has `job_limits: null` and a capped one does not, so the two are still told apart -- by a measurement rather than by a string.
claims.why: The comment refers to comparison of ledger entries; the code here only creates the attestation. No comparison logic is present in this chunk.

observations.what: log.verify() called; if it raises, exception propagates but token and token_sid are not cleaned up; they are local variables, so no resource leak.
subprocess.list2cmdline is used to quote argv; this is standard Python practice for Windows command lines.
On failure after job creation but before assignment, job handle is closed in except block; on success, job handle ownership is transferred to ContainedProcess.
TerminateProcess is called with exit code 1; if it fails, exception is caught and ignored; child process may remain running.
attestation.mechanism includes '+bounded-inherit' only if log is truthy; consistent with allowlist presence.
log.integrity_label and log.granted_access accessed only if log is not None; safe.
